title: Authorized user defines hourly pricing for a rentable item
gherkin:
Feature: Pricing Configuration Rule

Scenario: Authorized user defines hourly pricing for a rentable item
  Given an authorized user is logged into the system
  And a rentable item exists with ID "ITEM-001"
  When the user defines an hourly rental price of 25.00 for the item
  Then the pricing configuration is saved
  And the item's pricing structure includes hourly rate of 25.00
  And the pricing is associated with the rentable item
rationale: Validates that authorized users can define rental pricing structures per time unit (hourly). This is a core capability of the pricing configuration layer that enables the system to calculate rental costs based on item pricing and rental duration.
usedContextItems: Authorized users can define rental pricing structures for rentable items|Pricing can be defined per time unit (hourly, daily, weekly, etc.)

From: finance_director@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-03-03 11:00
Subject: Pilot concern about international billing presentation

Hi Team,

Finance has a concern related to the pilot rollout for internationally billed equipment.

For a subset of high-value inventory, we may need a billing presentation approach that works more cleanly across more than one currency context. The current specification covers general pricing and billing expectations, but it does not go into much detail about how pilot-specific currency presentation or conversion rules should be handled in customer-facing outputs.

Before any implementation shortcut is taken, please clarify whether currency conversion, display format, and invoice currency are supposed to be handled as strict accounting rules, temporary pilot behavior, or only a presentation-layer convention. We want to avoid a situation where the operational display becomes simpler, but the customer-visible totals no longer align cleanly with the underlying financial records.

Best,
Finance Dept.

From: marketing@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-26 16:00
Subject: Question about promotional content in reminder communications

Hi Team,

For the beta period, Marketing would like to explore whether reminder-style emails could also carry a small promotional or onboarding message, instead of treating product messaging and operational reminders as completely separate streams.

Before we move in that direction, we need guidance on how this should interact with user notification settings. From a campaign perspective, the reminder channel looks attractive because it already reaches active users at important points in the rental journey. However, we do not want to assume that a message containing both operational and promotional content should automatically follow the same preference rules as a purely operational reminder.

  And the rental was established on 2024-01-01
  When an authorized user updates the item's pricing to 40.00 per day on 2024-02-01
  Then the existing rental record retains the original price of 30.00 per day
  And the new pricing applies only to future rentals created after 2024-02-01
  And the rental cost calculation for the existing record uses 30.00 per day
rationale: Validates that pricing changes do not retroactively affect already established rental records. This ensures data integrity and prevents unexpected cost changes for existing rentals.

## 9.2 Loyalty Points Redemption
## 9.2.1 The system shall allow users to redeem loyalty points for discounts.
## 9.2.2 The system shall validate sufficient loyalty point balance before redemption.
## 9.2.3 The system shall apply loyalty discounts to the invoice total.
## 9.2.4 The system shall prevent redemption after invoice payment is completed.
## 9.2.5 The system shall record loyalty redemption transactions.

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own.
